lesson_title: Express Routing, Middleware, and API Flow

questions.question: Why does this route never run for requests to /jobs?
options: app.use() should only be used after all routes
The mounted router can intercept /jobs before the later route definition
GET routes cannot be used with app.use() in the same file
res.send() only works inside routers

questions.question: What is the bug in this middleware setup?
options: Middleware must be declared with function keyword only
next() is missing, so the request never reaches the route
console.log() blocks Express routes
GET routes must come before middleware

questions.question: Which object contains dynamic route params like /jobs/:id in Express?
options: req.body
req.headers
req.params
req.locals

questions.question: Why is this DELETE endpoint crashing when called?
options: DELETE routes cannot use params
The route param is named id, but the code reads req.params.jobId
res.json() cannot be used in DELETE handlers
The path should be /delete/jobs/:id

questions.question: Why does this API send 'Cannot set headers after they are sent'?
options: You are trying to send two responses for one request
res.json() must come after res.send()
GET routes can only send text, not JSON
Express requires status(200) before every response

questions.question: Why do we use middleware in Express?
options: To run logic like logging, auth, and parsing before the final route handler
To replace all route handlers with one function
To make Node.js run in the browser
To store data permanently without a database

questions.question: Why is this custom middleware not protecting the route?
options: next() still runs even after sending 401, so unauthorized users may continue
Authorization must be read from req.body
status(401) automatically calls next()
Middleware should not accept next as a parameter

questions.question: Why is this route not matching the expected URL?
options: The path is missing the leading slash
req.params only works with POST routes
Dynamic params require query strings instead
res.json() breaks dynamic routing

questions.question: What is wrong with this router export/import flow?
options: The router is never exported from jobs.routes.js and imported into app.js
Routers cannot be mounted with app.use()
router.get('/') should be router.get('/jobs')
Express routers only work in ES modules

questions.question: If a middleware sends a response, what should usually happen next?
options: Call next() anyway so later handlers also run
Stop the chain and return, because the request is already handled
Restart the middleware stack
Convert the response into req.body

questions.question: Why is req.query.search undefined when visiting /jobs?search=backend?
options: Query values should be read from req.query.search, not req.params.search
Express does not support query strings
search must be declared in the route path
Only POST routes can read query params

questions.question: Why is this async route likely to skip proper error handling?
options: Async route handlers should usually wrap awaited work in try/catch or use an error wrapper
await cannot be used inside Express routes
res.json() cannot send arrays
db.getJobs() must be called with next()
